beats.caption: Our exam project has a second part: a small experiment, separate from the quiz app.
beats.say: Our exam project has a second part: a small experiment, separate from the quiz app.

beats.caption: The assignment: let a linear regression model and a local language model with RAG predict the same number, then compare them.
beats.say: The assignment says: let a linear regression model, and a local language model with RAG, predict the same number. Then compare them.

beats.caption: First: what linear regression is. Then our task, our code, and the results.
beats.say: You do not need to know anything about machine learning. We start with what linear regression is. Then our task, our code, and the results.

beats.caption: In normal programming, a person writes the rule: input goes in, the rule runs, output comes out.
beats.say: In normal programming, a person writes the rule. Input goes in, the rule runs, output comes out.

beats.caption: In machine learning we give the computer examples of inputs with their correct outputs, and it finds the rule itself.
beats.say: In machine learning we turn that around. We give the computer examples, inputs together with their correct outputs, and it finds the rule itself.

beats.caption: Finding the rule is called training. The finished rule is called a model.
beats.say: Finding the rule is called training. The finished rule is called a model.

beats.caption: When the output is a number, such as a price, a temperature or a time, the job is called regression.
beats.say: When the output is a number, such as a price, a temperature or a time, the job is called regression.

beats.caption: Put every example on a chart: the input along the bottom, the output up the side. Each example is one dot.
beats.say: Put every example on a chart. The input goes along the bottom, the output goes up the side. Each example is one dot.

beats.caption: Linear regression draws the straight line that fits the dots best.
beats.say: Linear regression draws the straight line that fits the dots best.

beats.caption: A straight line is just two numbers: the slope (how steep) and the intercept (where it starts).
beats.say: A straight line is just two numbers. The slope says how steep it is. The intercept says where it starts.

beats.caption: Output = slope × input + intercept. Training means finding those two numbers.
beats.say: So the model is one small formula: output equals slope times input, plus intercept. Training means finding those two numbers.

beats.caption: To predict, take a new input, go up to the line, and read off the output.
beats.say: To predict, take a new input, go up to the line, and read off the output.

beats.caption: For each dot, measure how far the line is from it. That gap is the error.
beats.say: But which line is best? For each dot, measure how far the line is from it. That gap is the error.

beats.caption: Square every error and add them up. Squaring makes big misses count much more than small ones.
beats.say: Square every error and add them up. Squaring makes big misses count much more than small ones.

beats.caption: The best line is the one with the smallest total. This method is called least squares.
beats.say: The best line is the one with the smallest total. This method is called least squares, and the computer solves it in an instant.

beats.caption: A model can look good simply because it has already seen the answers.
beats.say: How do we know the model is any good? It can look good simply because it has already seen the answers.

beats.caption: So we split the data. The training set is used to fit the line. The test set is hidden until the end.
beats.say: So we split the data. The training set is used to fit the line. The test set is hidden until the end.

beats.caption: Then we predict the test cases and compare with the true values. The difference is the absolute error.
beats.say: Then we predict the test cases and compare with the true values. The difference, ignoring plus or minus, is the absolute error.

beats.caption: The average over all test cases is the mean absolute error, MAE. Lower is better.
beats.say: The average over all test cases is the mean absolute error. Lower is better.

beats.caption: Our task: predict how long a body takes to orbit the Sun, from its distance to the Sun.
beats.say: Now our task. We predict how long a body takes to go around the Sun, from its distance to the Sun.

beats.caption: Input: distance in astronomical units (Earth = 1 AU). Output: orbital period in Earth years.
beats.say: The input is the distance in astronomical units, where Earth is at one. The output is the orbital period in Earth years.

beats.caption: The data comes from the fact tables in the same NASA document the quiz app uses: nine bodies, Mercury to Pluto.
beats.say: The data comes from the fact tables in the same NASA document the quiz app uses. Nine bodies, from Mercury to Pluto.

beats.caption: We add a tenth, made-up body at 15 AU. The language model cannot have memorised it.
beats.say: We add a tenth, made-up body at fifteen astronomical units. The language model cannot have memorised that one.

beats.caption: Seven bodies are for training. Three are for testing: Mars, Uranus and the made-up body.
beats.say: Seven bodies are for training. Three are held back for testing: Mars, Uranus and the made-up body.

beats.caption: On a chart our data is not a straight line. It bends upward: far-away bodies take much longer.
beats.say: There is one problem. On a chart, our data is not a straight line. It bends upward: far-away bodies take much longer.

beats.caption: A straight line through that curve fits badly. For Mars it predicts minus 2.39 years.
beats.say: A straight line through that curve fits badly. For Mars it predicts minus two point four years, which is impossible.

beats.caption: The trick: take the logarithm of both numbers. A logarithm counts the size of a number: 10 becomes 1, 100 becomes 2.
beats.say: The trick is to take the logarithm of both numbers. A logarithm counts the size of a number: ten becomes one, one hundred becomes two.

beats.caption: On this log-log chart the same dots fall on a straight line, so linear regression fits.
beats.say: On this log-log chart, the very same dots fall on a straight line. Now linear regression fits.

beats.caption: The slope it finds is 1.4998. Kepler's third law says exactly 1.5: the model rediscovered the law from seven examples.
beats.say: The slope it finds is one point four nine nine eight. Kepler's third law of planetary motion says exactly one point five. The model rediscovered that law from seven examples.

beats.caption: Everything is in one file: experiment/run_experiment.py.
beats.say: Now the code. Everything is in one file: run experiment dot pie, in the experiment folder.

beats.caption: build_dataset() reads distance and orbit period from the PDF with two text patterns, converts the units, and marks each row train or test.
beats.say: The function build dataset reads the distance and the orbit period from the PDF with two text patterns, converts the units, and marks each row as train or test.

beats.caption: fit_regressions() gets the train rows. x is the distance, y is the period.
beats.say: The function fit regressions gets the train rows. X is the distance, Y is the period.

beats.caption: One line trains the model: LinearRegression().fit(), from the scikit-learn library, on the logarithms of x and y.
beats.say: One line trains the model. Linear regression, dot fit, from the sy-kit learn library, on the logarithms of X and Y.

beats.caption: A second model is fitted on the raw numbers, without logarithms, as a baseline to compare with.
beats.say: A second model is fitted on the raw numbers, without logarithms, as a baseline to compare with.

beats.caption: predict() gives the logarithm of the period, so 10 to that power turns it back into years.
beats.say: Predict gives the logarithm of the period. So ten to that power turns it back into years.

beats.caption: The other contestant is the local language model with RAG. It gets the same three test distances.
beats.say: The other contestant is the local language model with RAG. It gets the same three test distances.

beats.caption: build_store() writes one sentence per training body, with its distance and period, and saves them in a vector database.
beats.say: The function build store writes one sentence per training body, with its distance and its period, and saves them in a vector database.

beats.caption: The code then checks that no test body and no test answer is in that database, and stops if one is.
beats.say: The code then checks that no test body, and no test answer, is in that database. If one is, the program stops.

beats.caption: For each test case, run_cases() retrieves the 4 most similar sentences and puts them in the prompt as reference examples.
beats.say: For each test case, run cases retrieves the four most similar sentences and puts them in the prompt as reference examples.

beats.caption: The model must reply with a single number. We ask twice: with the examples, and without.
beats.say: The model must reply with a single number. We ask twice: once with the examples, and once without.

beats.caption: The language model never sees the regression, its two numbers, or any code. That keeps the comparison fair.
beats.say: The language model never sees the regression, its two numbers, or any code. That keeps the comparison fair.

beats.caption: Uranus takes 84.02 years. Log-log regression: 84.00. Straight-line baseline: 107.85.
beats.say: The results. Uranus really takes eighty-four point zero two years. The log-log regression says eighty-four point zero zero. The straight-line baseline says one hundred and eight.

beats.caption: The language model with RAG says 14.11 years. Without RAG it says 176.35.
beats.say: The language model with RAG says fourteen years. Without RAG it says one hundred and seventy-six.

beats.caption: Mean absolute error over the three test cases: 0.02 years for log-log regression, 17.24 for the baseline, 38.73 with RAG, 44.83 without.
beats.say: Over all three test cases, the mean absolute error is zero point zero two years for the log-log regression, seventeen for the baseline, thirty-nine for the language model with RAG, and forty-five without.

beats.caption: Regression is built for exactly this: it fits two numbers to a numeric pattern, and here the pattern is a straight line.
beats.say: Why such a gap? Regression is built for exactly this. It fits two numbers to a numeric pattern, and here the pattern really is a straight line.

beats.caption: The language model predicts likely words. It does not calculate, and it did not work out the pattern from four examples.
beats.say: The language model predicts likely words. It does not calculate, and it did not work out the pattern from four examples.

beats.caption: Retrieval did not help much: it finds similar text, not nearby numbers. The same four bodies came back for all three questions.
beats.say: And retrieval did not help much. It finds similar text, not nearby numbers. The same four bodies came back for all three questions.

beats.caption: A number that follows a pattern: train a small model. A fact you can quote from a document: use a language model with RAG.
beats.say: So the lesson is this. For a number that follows a pattern, train a small model. For a fact you can quote from a document, use a language model with RAG.

beats.caption: Honest limits: three test cases and one run. And the regression only works because we picked the right shape.
beats.say: Two honest limits. We had only three test cases and one run. And the regression only works this well because we picked the right shape for the data.
